clue.text: Brilliant detailed revenue lesson

indicators.note: de-tailed, with its tail cut off, so the last letter of the synonym for revenue goes

parts.note: revenue is income
a parable is a story that teaches a moral lesson

explanation.surface: Praise for a tax inspector's superb, thorough class on public finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as 'thorough' but means de-tailed: INCOME loses its final E to give INCOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brilliant is so outstanding that nothing else bears comparison with it.

clue.text: One impaled acquiring new cut

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: acquiring means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to be gored is to be impaled on horns

explanation.surface: A bullfight victim, freshly wounded, being sliced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquiring' puts N inside GORED, giving GNORED after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub them, deliberately pretending not to notice them.

clue.text: Believes what's seen at end of programme?

definitions.text: what's seen at end of programme?
definitions.meaning: the rolling list of cast and crew names shown after a film or TV show

explanation.surface: A viewer's faith in the closing titles of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Credits as a verb means accepts as true; as a noun it is the closing roll of names on screen.

clue.text: Tiny, oddly main nucleus spinning

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, the first and third, of the word main
spinning means the letters of nucleus are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: A physics picture: the core of an atom, oddly small, rotating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes M and I from main; 'spinning' turns NUCLEUS into NUSCULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Minuscule is a stronger synonym for very small, extremely little.

clue.text: African capital city referencing ants, initially

definitions.text: African capital city referencing ants, initially

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of each of the preceding words is taken

explanation.surface: A description of a West African capital somehow connected with insects.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, and its first letters spell it out too.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana in West Africa.

clue.text: One more from America, not here

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone saying another person arrived from the United States and isn't present.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the words: americA NOT HERe.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means an additional one, a further one of the same kind.

clue.text: Current contained by broken cattle grid

indicators.note: contained by means the first piece sits inside the second
broken means the letters of cattle are smashed into another order

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A farm scene: an electric current running through a damaged cattle grid.
explanation.walkthrough: A cattle grid is a British road barrier of bars that livestock won't cross. 'broken' rearranges CATTLE to LATTCE, and 'contained by' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a criss-cross framework of strips, a grid pattern.

clue.text: Eager moving round cities' haunts

indicators.note: moving round means the letters of the following words are shifted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A keen traveller getting around the haunts of various cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving round' is the anagram signal, applied to both following words together; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthusiastic means keenly interested and keen to take part, a synonym of eager.

clue.text: Old lady, impatient, possibly in buff

parts.note: nan is a familiar name for a grandmother, an old lady
keen means eager, impatient to get going

explanation.surface: An eager grandmother who might be found in the nude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in buff' suggests naked, but buff is the colour: nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth. 'possibly' admits that buff is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen, a cloth originally from Nanjing, is a pale yellowish-buff colour.

clue.text: Laugh with time left in job

indicators.note: in means the short pieces are placed inside the word for job

parts.note: a chore is a routine task or job

explanation.surface: Chuckling while killing time at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts T and L inside CHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chortle is a gleeful chuckle, a kind of laugh.

clue.text: Break in using crowbar? That's ingenious!

parts.note: to break in is to enter a building
prising is forcing something open with a lever such as a crowbar

explanation.surface: A burglar's crowbar entry admired as clever.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one burglary, but splits into two pieces: entering and prising.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprising means resourceful and inventive, showing initiative, close to ingenious.

clue.text: The woman's embracing university incels?

definitions.note: read as 'in cells': people who live alone in cells, a plural noun

indicators.note: embracing means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: hers is what belongs to the woman
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, a university

explanation.surface: A woman's university is full of involuntarily celibate men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incels' suggests involuntary celibates, but split it: 'in cells', where recluses and monks live. 'embracing' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Recluses living apart from the world traditionally dwell in cells, and are celibate too.

clue.text: Heretic cheers over robbery

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for cheers is read backwards

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: A nonbeliever celebrates after a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns TA into AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To believers an atheist, one who denies any god, is a heretic.

clue.text: Teams putting fish on board

indicators.note: on board means aboard a ship, so the fish goes inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, stands for a ship you go on board
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Football teams loading fish onto a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' means inside SS (steamship), a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Sides are opposing groups in a game, the teams.

clue.text: Bounder we arrested pocketing lingerie?

indicators.note: pocketing means the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A cad arrested with stolen ladies' underclothes in his pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the words: boUNDER WE ARrested. The question mark marks lingerie as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's undergarments, a type of what's worn beneath clothes.

clue.text: Remedy sipped, say, for indigestion

indicators.note: remedy as a verb means fix or put right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medicine taken in sips, supposedly for an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remedy' looks like a noun but is the verb: it rearranges SIPPED SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is the medical term for an upset stomach and poor digestion.

clue.text: Surfaces packed with endless sea doves?

definitions.note: doves in politics are peacemakers, plural like the answer

indicators.note: packed with means the outer word is filled with the other piece

parts.note: surfaces as a verb means comes into view, appears

indicators.note: endless means the word sea loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Pigeons rising out of the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surfaces' looks like a noun but is the verb; 'endless' trims the sea, and 'packed with' puts the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics doves favour peace and conciliation, so they placate opponents to avoid conflict.

clue.text: Sort of bridge game

definitions.meaning: a floating bridge supported on boats or drums
a card game where players aim for twenty-one, also called blackjack

explanation.surface: A kind of card game, bridge being one too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' tempts as the card game, but the first sense is a bridge over water.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating bridge rests on hollow floats; the card game of twenty-one has the same name.

clue.text: Perfect on gallery to see film

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: ace means excellent, perfect
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Visiting a gallery to watch a great movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate is a transparent plastic sheet, used as photographic and overhead projector film.

clue.text: Queen following top criminal act

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: a cap is a lid or top
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen trailing behind a mastermind crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top criminal' reads as a crime boss, but 'top' is CAP and 'criminal act' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is slang for a crime, typically an audacious robbery.

clue.text: Legend of trick encasing prone individual

indicators.note: encasing means wrapping around, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a con is a trick, a swindle
apt means likely or inclined, prone
I, the Roman one, stands for a single individual

explanation.surface: A myth about a con played on a gullible person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legend' suggests myth, but it means the words under a picture. 'encasing' puts APTI inside CON.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is the explanatory text accompanying a map or illustration.

clue.text: Made stink collaring waiter finally having forks

indicators.note: collaring means seizing and holding, so one piece is gripped within the other

parts.note: ponged is British slang for smelled bad

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of waiter is used

explanation.surface: A diner causes a stink and grabs the waiter by the collar over the cutlery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collaring' puts R inside PONGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronged means fitted with tines or points, like a fork.

clue.text: Deviation of entitled man after spank

indicators.note: after means the man comes behind the spank in the answer

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to spank them
a gent, short for gentleman, was a man of rank entitled to bear arms

explanation.surface: A privileged man going off the rails after being spanked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tan' is an old word for thrash, as in tanning someone's hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Going off on a tangent means veering away from the subject, a deviation.

clue.text: Indulgence of sweetheart in restaurant

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the word for restaurant

parts.note: trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Having a romantic dinner out with a loved one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' looks like a lover but splits as the heart of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat is a special pleasure or luxury, something indulged in.

clue.text: This compiler rejected game's uses

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the setter's word is read in reverse

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
a ploy is a game or stratagem, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: The setter, turned down, makes use of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Employs means puts to use, makes use of.

clue.text: Spoken English accompanying Church hymn

parts.note: oral means spoken

explanation.surface: A spoken English line alongside a church hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accompanying' just links the pieces; the church abbreviation comes first in the answer although it is last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorale is a stately hymn tune of the German Lutheran church.

clue.text: Small insect, beginning to nip, bit

parts.note: a midge is a tiny biting fly

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of nip is taken

explanation.surface: A little insect started to nip and then bit someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' looks like the past tense of bite, but it is a noun meaning a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgen is a tiny amount, a little bit.

clue.text: Arrest nude in frolics being abandoned

indicators.note: frolics means the letters cavort about into a new order

explanation.surface: Police ordered to arrest a naked person cavorting wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolics' rearranges ARREST NUDE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned behaviour is wild and uninhibited, with all restraint thrown off.
